title: Voters Are Not Polarized. They Are Up for Grabs.
gist: Zakaria argues that, contrary to the polarization narrative, U.S. and global electorates have weak loyalties and are shifting at record speed, citing Hispanic and youth swings away from Republicans and Lula's historic comeback in Brazil. He attributes Republican troubles to tariffs, the Iran war and affordability, and urges centrists to adopt a mixed left-right agenda including housing, AI tutoring and taxing capital over labor.

insights.claim: In Brazil, Lula trailed Flávio Bolsonaro by more than 2 million votes in the first round, then won 10 million more voters in three weeks to win the runoff handily, the first time a second-place first-round candidate has won in Brazilian presidential history.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Brazil's continued left-leaning government shapes fiscal and policy outlook for Brazilian assets.
insights.quote: Never before in Brazilian presidential elections had the candidate who came second in the first round been able to change enough minds to win in the final round.

insights.claim: Political movement that once took years can now happen in months or even weeks because we live in an age of anxiety.

insights.quote: But time has accelerated, and movement that took years can now happen in months, even weeks.
